prompt: Return all subsets of a set of up to 15 distinct numbers.
why: For each number choose in or out, recursing and undoing. 2ⁿ results, and n is small enough.
trap: When the output itself is exponential, no clever DP will save you.

prompt: Place n queens on an n×n board so that no two attack each other. Return every arrangement.
why: Place row by row, skip attacked columns and diagonals, undo and try the next column on failure.
trap: Greedy placement gets stuck; you need to undo choices.

prompt: List every combination of candidate numbers (reusable) that adds up to a target.
why: Recurse on the remaining target, trying each candidate from the current index on; stop below zero.
trap: DP can count the ways, but listing each one needs backtracking.

prompt: Does a word exist in a letter grid, formed by adjacent cells without reusing any cell?
why: DFS from each start cell, marking cells used on this path and unmarking on the way back.
trap: Plain flood-fill marks cells forever; here a cell is free again once you back out.

prompt: Given a string of phone digits, return all possible letter combinations they could spell.
why: Pick a letter for each digit in turn and recurse; every full pick is one answer.
trap: A trie is for checking words; here every combination counts.
